root_idea.summary: The root is oriented primarily toward emergence, rising, or being brought up and into motion; it also contains a distinct lexical branch for the bovine animal.
root_idea.development: The emergence principle extends to things rising or spreading, people or animals being roused, causative raising and stirring, and the cultivation or turning of earth. The bovine noun is treated as a separate lexical branch, with some figurative extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The QAC group represents Quran-attested Form IV forms whose normalized Classical Arabic citation form is أَثَارَ.

senses.definition: To raise, stir up, or cause to spread, especially dust or clouds.
senses.usage_conditions: Used causatively with dust, clouds, and similar phenomena; the Quranic contexts include raising dust and causing clouds to spread or rise.

senses.definition: To till or plough the land, turning up its soil.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with the earth or land in an agricultural construction; the Quranic usage concerns working and turning the ground rather than merely causing a visible cloud or dust to rise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise, become stirred or excited, or come into motion; of dust, smoke, redness, or similar things, to rise, appear, and spread; of a recumbent camel, bird, or swarm of locusts, to rise from its resting place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I verb covering emergence, rising, and becoming active in the constructions attested here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leap or spring toward someone or something; to rush upon or hasten to do evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with إِلَى or بِـ and related directional or adversarial constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gush or flow forth with force, said of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is flowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To appear or mount visibly, said of blood, especially when it rises into or mantles the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional bodily construction describing visible blood or flushing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break out, spread, or become manifest, said of measles, mouth-pustules, or fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for the outward appearance or flare-up of an illness or its symptoms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heave or become agitated, especially with a tendency to vomit, said of the soul or stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily reaction involving rising or agitation of the stomach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become aroused, inflamed, or sharply agitated, said of anger, discord, evil, or mischief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of emotional or social disturbance becoming active or spreading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To search, investigate, scrutinize, or inquire into an affair; to investigate the Quran and meditate on or seek knowledge of its meanings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Quran expression ثَوَّرَ القُرْآنَ denotes diligent investigation of its reading, interpretation, and meanings; this is a Form II usage and is not an additional QAC form group in the packet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leap upon, assault, or assail someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or directed assault construction, with the person attacked as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise, rouse, excite, or provoke a person, animal, or object; also to draw forth or disinter something buried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These broader causative uses include rousing a person or recumbent camel, stirring a pursued animal, and exhuming or digging up a buried thing; they are distinct from the Quranic cloud-and-dust and agricultural uses listed above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scrape up earth or dust with the legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a beast whose legs throw up the ground or dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To excite discord, dissension, evil, or mischief, and to bring it into manifestation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative social or moral construction with discord, evil, or mischief as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bull; also a cow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary animal noun, with the attested plural patterns belonging to this lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The constellation Taurus, one of the signs of the zodiac.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or conventional astronomical use of the bovine noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lord, master, chief, or leading person of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative honorific use; the evidence does not establish that it is a general title in every context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stupid, foolish, or dull person of little understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative characterization of a person as lacking sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person possessed by a devil, insane, or mad.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed figurative use equating the person with a state of possession or madness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or large piece of aqit, hardened and congealed milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A food noun distinct from the bovine meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The green growth covering stale water, or small rubbish and broken particles floating on its surface.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression ثَوْرُ المَاءِ refers to material lying on the surface of water; the sources record more than one interpretation of the cited poetic example.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pimples or small pustules breaking out in the mouth of a fevered person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily noun referring to an eruption in the mouth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The spreading redness appearing and rising above the horizon after sunset.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for the visible twilight glow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The white crescent or whiteness in the lower part of a person's nail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering or film over the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an opacity or layer lying upon the eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An excitement, upheaval, or state of agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting an active disturbance that may later become stilled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large number, great quantity, or abundance of people, wealth, camels, or similar things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quantitative noun; the evidence distinguishes abundance in general from the more specific wealth noun ثَرْوَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The body part called the خَوْرَان.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Emerging from the dust or earth, especially of locusts just coming forth before they have wings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression دَبًى ثَائِرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having hair that spreads out, stands up, or is shaggy and dishevelled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive expression for disordered hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the external jugular veins or neck sinews and veins swollen and prominent from anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily sign of anger or agitation, attested in a conventional descriptive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Angry or aroused to anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing a person in an angry state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anger, rage, or an ebullition of passion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized use, especially in the expression ثَارَ ثَائِرُهُ, whose meaning is that his anger became aroused or inflamed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ploughed-up land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial expression describing ground that has been turned by ploughing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land abounding in bulls or cows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive expression for land characterized by its bovine population.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cow that tills the ground; likewise, a bull used for tilling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial noun for a bovine employed in agricultural work.

lane_unit_coverage.note: General intransitive rising or becoming stirred.
Dust, smoke, redness, and other things rising, appearing, and spreading.
Recumbent camel becoming roused or moving.
Birds and locusts rising from where they lie.
Leaping or rushing toward someone or something.
Searching, investigating, and investigating Quranic meanings.
Causatively raising, rousing, exciting, or drawing forth.
A beast scraping up earth or dust.
Pointer-only cross-reference to a different headword.
Bovine noun and its astronomical extension.
Figurative stupid or dull person meaning.
Possessed, insane, or mad person meaning.
Green growth or debris on water.
Pustules in the mouth during fever.
Whiteness at the base of the nail.
Covering or film over the eye.
Land abounding in bulls or cows.

cautions: The QAC group contains inflected Form IV occurrences; the public headword is normalized to the perfect-tense citation form أَثَارَ.
The Quranic Form IV uses distinguish raising or spreading dust and clouds from tilling or turning the earth; contextual English glosses alone are not treated as separate senses.
The noun ثَوْرٌ includes a bovine branch distinct from the verbal emergence-and-raising branch.
